h: Make a whole Derbyshire day of it
p: Chatsworth has more than a few famous chapters in its story. Mary, Queen of Scots was held here more than once as a prisoner, in the care of the Earl of Shrewsbury, husband of the formidable Bess of Hardwick, who built the first great house on the site. Centuries later, the house played Mr Darcy's Pemberley in the 2005 film of Pride and Prejudice, so film fans might get a little thrill walking up to the front.

Give yourself a full day here. The house, the garden and the farmyard can all eat up hours on their own, and the parkland is free to wander, which makes it a lovely spot for a riverside walk or a picnic. If you've got energy to spare, head up into Stand Wood behind the house for big views back across the estate. Look out for the Hunting Tower poking up through the trees.
Christmas is a particularly big deal at Chatsworth, with the house dressed up in themed decorations each year and a festive market, so it's worth looking at what's on if you're visiting in winter.

Nearby, the estate village of Edensor is a picture-postcard spot just across the park, and the Chatsworth Estate Farm Shop at Pilsley is a treat for foodies. Bakewell is only a few miles away for a wander round the town and, of course, a Bakewell pudding or tart. History lovers can pair Chatsworth with Haddon Hall, another cracking medieval manor house just the other side of Bakewell.
